title: Restrict server-side requests to intended destinations
summary: When the server fetches a URL that a user, integration, or model can influence, the destination must be constrained so the request cannot reach internal services, cloud metadata endpoints, or arbitrary hosts.
review_checks: Find HTTP clients whose URL, host, or redirect target comes from request data, stored records, webhooks, or model output.
Check whether the destination is validated after DNS resolution and after every redirect.
Check whether response bodies or timing are returned to the caller.
safe_tests: Point the feature at a local listener on 127.0.0.1 and confirm the request is refused.
Use a hostname that resolves to a private or link-local address and confirm it is refused, including through a redirect.
remediation: Prefer identifiers over URLs: accept a document or integration ID and build the URL server-side.
Otherwise enforce an allowlist of schemes and hosts, resolve the host once, reject loopback, private, link-local, and metadata ranges, and connect to the vetted address.
Disable automatic redirects or re-validate each hop; cap response size and do not echo raw responses to the caller.
